newsitem.title: UZBEKISTAN: IMF's Fischer arrives for talks in Uzbekistan.
newsitem.headline: IMF's Fischer arrives for talks in Uzbekistan.

text.p: Stanley Fischer, deputy managing director of the International Monetary Fund, arrived in the Uzbek capital Tashkent on Friday for talks with President Islam Karimov, a fund source said.
"Fischer has arrived," the source, who declined to be identified, said.

The IMF suspended a $185 million loan to the former Soviet republic late last year, criticising the imposition of foreign exchange controls and Uzbekistan's failure to meet the fund's inflation targets.
Last week, Uzbek officials said Fischer had been invited by the government to try and improve relations with the IMF.
No details on the substance of the talks have been made public but observers say Uzbekistan's foreign exchange controls are likely to top the agenda.

The source said Fischer would meet Karimov, finance minister Bakhtier Khamidov and Central Bank chairman Faizullo Mulladzhanov on Friday. On Saturday, he is also scheduled to meet Rustam Azimov, chairman of the National Bank for Foreign Economic Activity, and address a banking forum.
Earlier this week, businessmen and diplomats said they doubted the visit would see any quick end to exchange controls.
Desperate for cash to bail out the troubled agriculture sector, the government imposed the exchange controls late last year following disastrous cotton and wheat harvests.

The controls have created a flourishing black market in dollars, with the so-called "bazaar rate" at around 145 sums to the dollar, way above the official exchange rate of about 60 sums to the dollar.
There is also a routine IMF mission visit underway in Uzbekistan which will last until May 13.
